newsitem.title: USA: Agouron says Viracept trial begins.
newsitem.headline: Agouron says Viracept trial begins.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc on Monday said a clinical trial of its HIV protease inhibitor Viracept, or nelfinavir mesylate, has started at the Terry Beirn Community Programs for Clinical Research on AIDS.

The trial will evaluate and compare HIV progression and death in patients taking either Viracept in combination with nucleoside analogues such as AZT, 3TC, ddI, ddC, d4T, or Norvir plus nucleoside analogues. Norvir is also known as ritonavir.
Agouron shares were up 1-3/8 to 72 by midday.

The study also will compare the two treatment groups for rates of adverse events or discontinuation from the study, as well as changes in CD4+ T-cells and plasma HIV RNA, Agouron said in a statement. The study will include 1,300 people with CD4+ T-cells of less than or equal to 100 cells/mm3.

Enrollment has begun at Terry Beirn Community Programs throughout the United States, which is funded by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a branch of the National Institutes of Health.The Canadian HIV Trials Network will be collaborating on the study.

In December, Agouron announced its submission of a new drug application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration covering tablet and pediatric powder formulations of Viracept. Regulatory submissions are expected in Canada and Europe later this year.
